## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been dealing with it for so long. Before you quit tomorrow, can we talk through what’s been happening and what you’d want to do next? You don’t have to make the decision alone or tonight. If the situation is seriously affecting your health or safety, getting some space may be important—but let’s make sure you have a plan for money, notice, and what comes after.

## 2

I understand why some images might seem suspicious, especially when they come from unfamiliar sources, but the evidence that Earth is round doesn’t depend on a single photograph. We can observe ships disappearing over the horizon, see different stars from different parts of the world, measure Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, and track satellites and weather systems. Independent space agencies, universities, private companies, and amateur observers all make observations that fit a spherical Earth. Faking all of that consistently would be far more complicated than explaining the evidence itself.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors, like the colors in a rainbow. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny air molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more easily than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from across the sky.

Violet is scattered even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to violet, and some violet light is absorbed high in the atmosphere. That is why the sky usually looks blue. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, scattering much of the blue away and leaving more reds and oranges for us to see.

## 4

雨落在深夜的屋檐上，细密而持续，像有人轻轻敲打着一面旧鼓。街灯被水汽晕成朦胧的黄色，空荡的路面映着摇曳的光。窗外偶尔驶过一辆车，轮胎卷起水花，很快又消失在远处。屋里只亮着一盏小灯，茶杯冒出的热气缓缓升起。雨声隔开了城市的喧闹，也让这个夜晚显得安静而温柔，仿佛时间暂时停在了玻璃窗上。
